q: Is grid-charged battery backup lower carbon than running a DG set during power cuts?
title: Battery backup or DG set: which emits less?
short: Usually yes, and clearly so when the DG set runs at light load. Battery backup emits 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh divided by its round-trip efficiency, about 0.81 kg at 88 percent. A DG set emits 2.68 kg per litre divided by kWh per litre: 0.89 kg at 3 kWh per litre, 1.34 kg at 2.
audience: MSME owners and commercial building managers

ul: Battery: kg CO2 per kWh delivered = 0.710 / round-trip efficiency. The losses are extra grid kWh, so they count.
DG set: kg CO2 per kWh delivered = 2.68 / kWh generated per litre of diesel, from your own fuel and energy meter readings.

p: A DG set sized for the whole plant often carries a small backup load during a cut, and its kWh per litre drops sharply below about half load. Read litres per kWh from your logbook for actual cut hours, not the data sheet at 75 percent load. At light load the battery wins clearly; at good load the two can be close.

sections.h: What the battery side must include
ul: Round-trip efficiency from the manufacturer for the actual chemistry: lithium systems usually do better than older lead-acid inverter banks.
Standby losses: charger, inverter idle draw and self-discharge, which add grid kWh even on days without a cut.
If the battery is charged from rooftop solar that would otherwise be exported, those kWh carry no grid emissions, which lowers the battery figure further.

p: Diesel burnt in your own DG set is Scope 1. Grid power used to charge the battery is Scope 2. Switching from DG to batteries moves emissions from Scope 1 to a smaller Scope 2 figure, so report both lines rather than a single net change.

example.title: Worked example: 12,000 kWh of backup a year
lines: Battery at 88% round-trip efficiency (assumed): 12,000 / 0.88 = 13,636 grid kWh
DG set at 2.2 kWh per litre during cuts (assumed from logbook): 12,000 / 2.2 = 5,455 L
Difference: 14,619 minus 9,682 = 4,937 kg, about 4.9 t CO2 a year lower with the battery
example.note: Add standby losses to the battery side if the charger runs all year.

senseible: Senseible calculates both sides from your bills: diesel invoices at 2.68 kg CO2 per litre as Scope 1 and grid kWh at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh (CEA version 21.0) as Scope 2, so the shift shows up in the monthly record.
